findings.anchor: _proxy_terminate_and_finalize: db.update_execution_status(execution_id=task_execution_id, status=CANCELLED) with no agent check; fix: entry gate in terminate_execution
findings.title: Cross-agent false-cancel through the proxy terminate arm via caller-supplied task_execution_id
findings.description: terminate_execution takes execution_id (path) and task_execution_id (query param, defaults to the path id). The proxy arm POSTs execution_id to agent A — whose 404 is what scoped the old path — but writes CANCELLED and closes the dispatch activity keyed on task_execution_id, which the agent never sees. The #2433 review added agent-scope belts to the queued and parked arms; the independent verifier found the proxy arm carried none.
exploit_scenario: Caller is authorised on agent A and has a live turn X on A.
Caller learns agent B's execution id T (128-bit; learnable from the fleet-wide /ws agent_activity stream — see below_gate #1).
Queued arm: B's row is not queued/not A's → None. Parked arm: registry/marker scoped to A → None.

Proxy arm: agent A answers terminated for X; release_if_matches(A, T) is a no-op; db.update_execution_status(T, CANCELLED) wins the CAS on B's RUNNING row; B's dispatch activity is closed as cancelled.
B keeps running (never contacted) but its later SUCCESS loses the CAS: B's deliverable is discarded and its row reads as a user cancellation.
findings.impact: Cross-tenant false-cancel + result loss on any agent whose execution id is known; no slot release, no process kill, no RCE.
findings.recommendation: FIXED: one agent-scope gate at the entry of terminate_execution for all three arms — the row behind task_execution_id must belong to name (uniform 404 'Execution not found in agent', so a foreign id reads like an unknown one; an unreadable row fails closed with 503); per-arm belts kept as a second layer. Tests: test_2433_dispatch_wiring.py (exploit replay, fail-closed, positive controls).
findings.verification: Independent fresh-context verifier (Phase 12) refuted the branch's 'closed on all arms' claim with a traced exploit; the entry gate was added and the exploit test now passes; test_ent155_chat_cancel.py and test_terminate_async_executor.py unchanged and green.

below_gate.item: /ws (SCOPE_ALL) broadcasts agent_activity events carrying execution_id / related_execution_id / agent_name fleet-wide to any authenticated user, so an execution id is learnable without access to its agent
below_gate.why_below: pre-existing, documented thin-trigger design outside this diff; with finding 1 fixed the id alone is no longer a write capability. Residual: cross-tenant disclosure of ids, agent names and activity types. Recommend a follow-up to scope /ws agent_activity by accessible_agents like /ws/events.

below_gate.item: pending_ids is agent-asserted (a compromised agent can claim any id)
below_gate.why_below: the watchdog unions it only against that agent's OWN rows (cleanup_service._extract_agent_known_ids, type-guarded), so the blast radius is 'keep my own rows alive', which the agent could already do by running them.

below_gate.item: Path-supplied execution ids reach Redis as key material (execution:cancel:{id})
below_gate.why_below: keys are binary-safe bulk strings (no protocol injection) and the cancel key is written only after the marker's agent matches the caller's authorised agent; no unbounded key creation.
